name: Arcade
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Build an interactive product story from captured screens and hotspots

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 user; 1 published interactive demo plus 1 video; unlimited views; 200 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Up to 10 users; unlimited demos and videos; 800 AI credits/month; 1 brand kit
tiers.notes: The supplied snapshot said $38/month for Pro; the current self-serve paid tier is Growth at $50 monthly or $42.50/month annually.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, demos, security and support; up to 10 brand kits and 100,000 AI credits/year

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user, 1 published interactive demo, 1 published video, unlimited views and 200 AI credits/month
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; paid creators are seat-based
pricing.hiddenCosts: Videos and generated visuals consume credits, roughly 50 credits per 30 seconds of video or per generated visual, while each additional creator requires a paid seat.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Arcade, build an interactive product story from captured screens and hotspots. The hard boundary is capture polish, hosted playback, analytics, personalization, and collaboration, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Capture a screen or window with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments with hotspots into an interactive product story, and export a shareable local video.
whatYouLose: capture polish, hosted playback, analytics, personalization, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Arcade because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Propels
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Open-source in theory; 27 stars and an AWS Amplify development setup are not a product a non-builder installs.

rejectedAlternatives.name: rrweb
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous answer is an SDK and player, not a product anyone can install and hand to sales.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Arcade in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture a screen or window with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments with hotspots into an interactive product story, and export a shareable local video.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
